- When sentiment is negative or near-zero in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for such periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.6 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to overfit upward trend; cap forecast growth at 2–4% per day unless sentiment is sustained.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is weak or mixed (e.g., <0.4), especially in early days of forecast horizon; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period volatility; adjust final 5–7 days downward if sentiment turns negative or shows divergence from prior 10-day trend.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.3 → +0.4), model tends to lag; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment shift.
